tools.title: 50/30/20 Rule
tools.description: Divide net income into 50% essentials (Needs), 30% lifestyle (Wants), and 20% future security (Savings).

tools.title: Budget Calculator
tools.description: Input real income, planned fixed expenses, flexible expenses, and savings targets to analyze your monthly financial health.

tools.title: Guiding Questions
tools.description: Answer 5 strategic diagnostic questions to identify your financial posture, key leakage points, and immediate next steps.

tools.title: Budget Planner
tools.description: Build and customize your monthly line-item budget table. Add entries, categorize them, and track remaining allocations live.

tools.title: Saving Goals
tools.description: Define specific targets, track current funds, calculate time to completion, and see visual progress meters.

guidingQuestions.question: What is your typical monthly net income?
guidingQuestions.subtitle: Include all regular take-home earnings (allowance, salary, stipend, predictable gigs).
guidingQuestions.hint: Be conservative: only enter money you are sure to receive.

guidingQuestions.question: What are your total essential expenses (Needs)?
guidingQuestions.subtitle: Rent/hostel, basic groceries, utilities, tuition, and required transportation.
guidingQuestions.hint: Items your daily survival or academic commitments rely upon.

guidingQuestions.question: What do you typically spend on lifestyle choices (Wants)?
guidingQuestions.subtitle: Cafe visits, food delivery, streaming entertainment, shopping, hobby gear.

guidingQuestions.question: How much do you currently manage to save each month?
guidingQuestions.subtitle: Money set aside into an account or cash envelope that is not spent.
guidingQuestions.hint: Even small recurring sums count toward this total.

guidingQuestions.question: What is your primary savings goal right now?
guidingQuestions.subtitle: Select the immediate milestone you are working toward.
options: Tech / Study Equipment (Laptop, tablet, course tools)
guidingQuestions.hint: Focusing on one primary goal prevents dilution of effort.
